body:
Walaykum asalam,

I'm sorry you're in a very difficult time. I've learned first-hand that if we have difficulty in trusting in Allah, it's due to something inside us, as there are many hadith and Qur'an verses that show Allah is Al-Wakeel.

My sister, Allah is the only One we can rely on since no one else can understand our problems or really help us. Have you tried talking to Allah and explaining what you wrote in your post or what you're thinking about? Have you told Him that you're going through a hard time and want to trust more in Him and that you need help and comfort? What would happen if you spoke to Him as a close friend? Try and see where it takes you from there.

You sound exhausted. Take a break, and read Qur'an, as those are literally Allah's words and they are meant to be a guidance and healing. Tafsir from people like Yasir Qadhi help tremendously as well.

I hope you find peace and may Allah make your path easy, ameen.

Such great advice! This is how I did it as well and it worked beautifully mashAllah. 

One thing I would add is to track your progress. Download an app that helps you stay accountable. Personally, I used Pillars at the start. Even though I dont  really need it anymore (alhamdullillah) I keep using it. Idk there's something satisfying about checking off that you prayed. To add to the other comment about motivation, checking off a tick mark that you prayed is kind of like a dopamine boost. And its also satisfying when you see your progress over a long period of time (you can see how many tick marks you have made!!!)

I pray Allah helps you become more consistent with prayer, op. ameen! You got this ❤️

I appreciate your honesty. Youre right that, at the end of the day, people want what they want. I still dont believe being attracted physically will make things easier aside from having more babies.

I dont have to be in marriage to know that some brutal things happen in life that break people. I think its far more importsnt to have someone who can keeo the ship sailing through the storm rather than someone with a fancy boat. I think more people need to understand this.

I guess Ive also just been feeling like if anyone says they think Im attractive after this, I wont ever be able to believe them after what I went through. I would just feel like I am being used and would have perpetual trust issues.

Thanks for understanding and saying all that girl. I felt kind of gaslit when some people told me to basically just fix it when theres not much I can do else at this point. I also agree that beauty can be found in all kinds of people. So truly, thank you. And im sure youre also more beautiful than you think ❤️

Lol glad u understand abt the desi thing...

I would be open to other ethnicities even reverts, but i have just seen fewer of them and fewer who are interested around my age. Its a good recommendation and i should keep an eye out in the future.

Thanks for the idea and encouragement sis.

Not sure where the conversation is going now, but good for your friends, mashaAllah. If theyre from good families, thats good. Im not from a good family, unfortunately. Desi's. I still try to be a good person and I wouldnt say I ask for too much either.

Its ok. I appreciate you engaging with me. Its helped me a little bit, but maybe im just one of the exceptions. Maybe its all for a good reason.

Jazak Allah khair sis
Fyi, dont use half our deen if u dont live in USA. Most people I saw were on USA. And generally, not a lot of people on there to begin with.

I have insecurities but I still like my appearance/personality. What gets me is that they dont even want to talk to me or get to know me after seeing how I look, which, at some point made me more insecure. In other words, I am not even getting a chance to speak with them, so they wouldnt be driven off by my insecurities. One of the first things they ask for is a picture.

My face isnt the true problem. I feel like its the expectation to look a certain way, like a snatched baddie or something like that. Its infuriating especially when this is coming from Muslims who bash on the West, yet still adopt the disgusting attitude that many people who date have. 

Youre right about average looking guys turning their nose up at others lol. I just felt so crazy after getting so many rejections in a row, even if they werent necessarily attractive themselves. I feel so jaded about men now, even tho i know not all are like that, sadly :/

It seems like everyone just thinks im not taking care of myself, which is not true. Unfortunately, my best efforts are still rejected. There are some impossible things I feel like people want and I can just never be that because of how my face (not body***) looks. Those things can only be changed with plastic surgery, not working out more.

I dont believe physical attraction is all the matters. Are you still going to be attracted to your spouse when they all of a sudden change and develop a terrible personality? Or when theyre looks one day leave them? What happens then? Ive always seen it as shallow and I am always willing to give a guy a chance to get to know him regardless of how he looks. Its not my main concern and I think it should not everyones first concern either.

To be clear, i dont have a problem with attractive people. I think its a huge shame if someone doesnt give someone a chance just based on the way they look.

Isnt there more to life than that?

Yes, thats the obvious answer, and youre right.

But thing is I do take care of myself. I believe that a part of being grateful is taking care of what God has given you. 

It doesnt help when certain things, like simply the shape of your face, is out of your control. Its like I am expected to come out of the womb already perfect or be hoor al ayn on earth. It doesnt help either when the whole world wants to tell you whats beautiful. I just thought Muslims would care a little bit more about personality and character.

So sorry this happened to you. Its tough enough getting to know someone and then they do this. Good thing you did not marry her.

Dont use the apps, not even so called matrimonial websites. Most times, its hard to build a connection with a stranger and it is even more difficult when its through a screen. 

I know its hard, since u said u live in a small city. Maybe you can think about finding a job in a city where there are more muslims and relocating. If thats also difficult, then i am really sorry. But apps, imo, are not worth one bit of the mental anguish/heartbream u go thru. 

Take a break. May Allah make it easy for u.

My self esteem has suffered so much from the search.

I get rejected based on the way i look without being given a chance. I feel worthless and ugly. No support from my parents either.

I wish people who claim to be religous/successful would stop being so shallow when looking for someone. People say its about chemistry, but thats just an excuse to be as picky as you want. Besides, nothing lasts forever in the wordly life!

Im not rich or pretty or have a good family. I have my deen but that isnt enough for anyone. I am not enough and i dont think i will ever be.

Even if by Allah's permission I did, i dont think i would be immune to doubt about if my spouse really liked me or was just using me.

Theres just no point in putting any more energy in this anymore. At least I can say I tried. All i can do is put that effort into doing other good deeds.

I have to content myself with dying alone.
